solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One's live, on air, turning up in European countries

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word air is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A broadcast goes out live across several countries of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' works on the word air; in a down entry it reads from the bottom upwards. Iberia is the peninsula, not a single country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, so it stands for those nations together.

clue.text: Problem having no opening item for broadcast? It leads to scratching

indicators.note: the first letter is lost from the synonym for problem

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

indicators.note: broadcast seeds are scattered, so the letters of item are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A broadcaster has trouble with the first item on the running order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no opening' drops the H of HITCH, leaving ITCH; 'for broadcast' rearranges ITEM into MITE.
explanation.definitionFit: The itch mite is the tiny parasite behind scabies, whose burrowing makes the sufferer scratch.

clue.text: Rugby game still appearing in sections

indicators.note: one word turns up inside the other, so the synonym for still is placed within SS

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for sections, as in a legal document
still water is even, calm and flat

explanation.surface: A rugby match is still being shown in parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is the seven-a-side short form of rugby union played at tournaments.

clue.text: Uncover rear having brought a vehicle in? It's a piece of cake

indicators.note: with the next word, says something has been brought inside the first piece
completes the container signal: a car is taken inside the prank

parts.note: to moon is to bare one's bottom as a prank
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone bares their backside after bringing a vehicle into it, an absurd picture ending with cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having brought ... in' is a split container signal: the vehicle goes inside the bottom-baring word after its first letter. To moon is British and American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond or coconut sweet bake, a little cake or biscuit.

clue.text: Border country not up for recall, a plateau

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word for not up is read backwards

parts.note: someone not up is still abed, lying in bed
a tableland is a raised flat plateau

explanation.surface: A border region's referendum on recalling its leader is held on high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for recall' turns ABED into DEBA, which is followed by TABLELAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The Debatable Land was the disputed strip on the Anglo-Scottish frontier, claimed by both kingdoms.

clue.text: Greeted Anglo-Chinese style, say,/showing some weightiness?

definitions.meaning: chin-chin is an old Anglo-Chinese greeting or toast, so someone greeted that way has been chinned twice over
a plump person has a fold of flesh beneath the jaw

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun on chin-chin, a pidgin greeting brought back from China.
explanation.definitionFit: A second fold under the jaw is a classic sign of carrying extra weight.

clue.text: Very substantial binging aboard when at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Passengers on a cruise eat to excess while afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges BINGING ABOARD; this grid takes the spelling those thirteen letters give rather than the fuller Brobdingnagian.
explanation.definitionFit: Brobdingnag is the land of giants in Gulliver's Travels, so its adjective means huge or gigantic.

clue.text: Set parts of targets in German article on crime

indicators.note: the target parts are placed inside the German article

parts.note: der is the masculine definite article in German
inners are the rings just outside the bull on an archery or shooting target
vice is wrongdoing, crime

explanation.surface: A German newspaper article runs on target practice and crime.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry 'on' puts VICE beneath DINNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of matching plates and dishes for a meal is a single collection, so set is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Sound of engine backing up beside expensive car

indicators.note: to back is to go in reverse, so the word up is read backwards

parts.note: RR is short for Rolls-Royce, a costly luxury car

explanation.surface: An engine's note as a luxury car reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothly running motor is said to hum softly like a contented cat.

clue.text: Dance Tannoy one repaired after end of ceilidh

indicators.note: the shuffled loudspeaker letters come after the ceilidh's last letter
the final letter of ceilidh is taken
something repaired is put back together, here in a different order

explanation.surface: At a Scottish dance the loudspeaker is fixed once the evening ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges the two words Tannoy one. A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social evening of folk dancing; a Tannoy is a British public-address loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal folk party with music and dancing, a lively social gathering.

clue.text: Hack's latest article accepted by everyone on Independent — it's basic stuff

indicators.note: the letters are taken in by the word for everyone

parts.note: everyone is all

indicators.note: the final letter of the word hack is used

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A journalist's newest piece is taken by every Independent reader, though it's nothing elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: KA goes inside ALL, then I follows. 'basic' is the chemist's sense, not 'simple'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkali is a base in chemistry, a substance with pH above seven.

clue.text: Find/time to return to the CD player?

definitions.meaning: to find something is to come upon it, unearth it

definitions.text: time to return to the CD player
definitions.meaning: when a disc is over, its playing has finished and one goes back to the machine

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as two words: a disc being over.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something new or hidden is to come upon it for the first time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Result of drink company's introduction of flat charge, with reasons

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: the opening letter of flat is taken

parts.note: a fee is a charge
grounds are reasons, justifications

explanation.surface: A firm brings in a flat-rate charge and gives its reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grounds are the spent dregs left behind once the brew has been made and poured.

clue.text: Look up in writing names of ticket recipients

indicators.note: the turned look is placed within the word for writing

parts.note: fist is an informal word for handwriting

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly

explanation.surface: Someone checks a written list of who is getting tickets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the look word in this down entry; fist as handwriting is an old informal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A free list is a register of people given complimentary tickets to a show.

clue.text: Musician sang trio with ornamentation

indicators.note: ornamented music is embellished and elaborated, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A musician sang a trio with plenty of decorative flourishes.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist is a musician who plays the organ, often in church.

clue.text: Manic flicks capturing historic time in Hollywood technology

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold another piece inside them
to flick something is to flip it about, so the letters of manic are thrown into a new order

parts.note: an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: Frantic films with a historical period setting, in Hollywood style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flicks' rearranges manic, and the period goes inside after the third letter. 'Flicks' looks like films, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerama was a 1950s widescreen projection system using three cameras and a curved screen.

clue.text: TV journalist's article: hard work (left unfinished)

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for hard work is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a tedious, hard task

explanation.surface: A television reporter's piece was hard going and never completed.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the presenter who fronts a news broadcast, linking reports, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: Rule? Here's foremost of generals ruling last of militiamen

indicators.note: the first letter of generals is used

parts.note: one ruling a people is over them

indicators.note: the final letter of militiamen is used

explanation.surface: Here the generals are in charge of the militia's rear ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule a country or people, a direct synonym verb.

clue.text: One turning out, not getting first place? Yes and no

definitions.text: One turning out, not getting first place? Yes and no

indicators.note: the opening letter is not included

parts.note: an evictor turns tenants out of their home

explanation.surface: A competitor knocked out of the race fails to come first, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' admits the joke: the result does get first place, though built by losing a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor is a winner, the one who comes first, which the clue both denies and affirms.

clue.text: Tone of voice: what one catches around start of line

indicators.note: the illness word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: an infection is something caught, like a cold

indicators.note: the first letter of line is taken

explanation.surface: A voice coach notes how a speaker's tone catches at the start of each line.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflection is the rise and fall in pitch of the voice when speaking.

clue.text: An example of film/speed

definitions.meaning: an extract shown from a movie, a short excerpt
a good ... is a brisk pace, as in moving at a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A short excerpt of film is one sense; a brisk rate of movement is the other.

clue.text: Reduction on pack amongst various reductions here?

parts.note: a discount is a reduction in price
to store something is to pack it away

explanation.surface: A cut-price deal on a pack sits among many other bargains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-price shop is the place where shoppers find themselves surrounded by markdowns on goods.
